title: Getting Ready for a Closer Look

patient.name: Mr Goh ChinAnn
patient.presenting_complaint: Diabetic eye screening — referred by polyclinic for annual diabetic retinopathy check

history.hpc: Mr Goh is attending for his annual diabetic eye screening as referred by his polyclinic. The doctor has reviewed his VA and IOP and ordered pupil dilation in both eyes so the fundus can be examined for signs of diabetic retinopathy. Mr Goh drove himself to the clinic and mentions he needs to drive back to work after this appointment.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years, HbA1c last checked at 7.8%. No previous eye surgery. No known glaucoma.
history.family_hx: Father has type 2 diabetes and diabetic retinopathy.
history.social_hx: Drove himself to the appointment. Works as a warehouse supervisor — job involves operating a forklift.

examination_findings.fundus: Pending — to be examined by doctor after dilation

pupil_dilation.dilating_drops_used: Tropicamide 1% and phenylephrine 2.5%, one drop each, both eyes
pupil_dilation.number_of_instillations: 1 instillation of each drop per eye, repeated once after 10 minutes as pupils were not yet adequately dilated
pupil_dilation.time_taken: Drops instilled at time of documentation; pupils re-checked after 20-25 minutes before sending for fundus exam

diagnosis: Both eyes prepared for fundus examination via pupil dilation as ordered by the doctor for diabetic retinopathy screening. Patient counselled on temporary visual effects of dilation and driving safety. Pending doctor's fundus assessment.

immediate: Confirm the order for dilation — both eyes (DBE) — and the diagnosis/indication (diabetic retinopathy screening) before proceeding
Confirm patient identity and check for any known allergies to dilating drops
Document pre-dilation pupil size for both eyes (RE and LE) in mm
Explain the procedure: 'I will put two types of eye drops in each eye to widen your pupils so the doctor can examine the back of your eyes properly.'

Instil tropicamide 1% and phenylephrine 2.5%, one drop of each in both eyes, using correct technique (tilt head back, pull down lower lid, instil in lower fornix, gentle eye closure with nasolacrimal occlusion)
Document the number of instillations and the time given
Re-check pupil size after about 10-15 minutes; if not adequately dilated, repeat the drops as needed and document the repeat instillation and time
Before the patient leaves the waiting area, ask specifically: 'How did you get here today — did you drive?'

Since Mr Goh drove himself, advise him clearly that his vision will be blurred and light-sensitive for 4-6 hours and he should not drive until this resolves — discuss arranging alternative transport home and to work
follow_up: Once pupils are adequately dilated, escort or direct the patient to the consultation room for the doctor's fundus examination
Document the final pupil size and time of adequate dilation in SCM
Inform the doctor or nurse that the patient drove himself and has been counselled about not driving post-dilation
patient_education: Explain that his near vision will be blurred and his eyes will be sensitive to bright light for approximately 4-6 hours after dilation
Sunglasses can help with light sensitivity — offer disposable sunglasses if available at the clinic
Strongly advise against driving until the effects wear off — suggest he arrange a colleague, family member, or public transport/taxi for his return journey
Reassure him that this is a routine and temporary part of the diabetic eye screening process

key_points: Confirms the dilation order, indication, and which eye(s) to dilate before proceeding
Checks for known allergies to dilating drops before instillation
Documents pre-dilation pupil size for both eyes
Proactively asks how the patient travelled to the clinic — identifies the driving safety issue
Uses correct dilating drops (tropicamide 1% and phenylephrine 2.5%) and correct instillation technique
Documents number of instillations and time given for each round of drops
Re-checks pupil size and repeats drops if dilation is inadequate, documenting the repeat
Records all findings (pre-dilation size, drops used, timing) accurately for the doctor
Recognises that pupil dilation is preparation for the doctor's fundus exam, not a diagnostic step itself
Identifies driving as a safety risk after dilation given the patient drove himself
Does not comment on the patient's diabetic retinopathy risk or fundus findings, as these are not yet examined
Understands the link between diabetes duration/control and the indication for screening, without diagnosing
Counsels the patient clearly about post-dilation visual effects (blurred near vision, photosensitivity, duration)
Proactively addresses the driving safety issue and suggests practical alternatives
Offers practical comfort measures (e.g., sunglasses) for light sensitivity
Communicates dilation status and driving counselling to the doctor/nurse before handover
